title: gusto job.json, version 1
description: The spec at the root of a job directory. It carries a brief, not a prompt. A reader fills in ref, sensitivity and budget when they are left out, and ignores a field it does not know. `gusto new` writes every field except model, which it leaves out when empty.

version.description: The format of this file. A file without it is version 1. A reader refuses a version newer than it knows.

brief.description: What to do, in a person's words. It is input to the harness, which the adapter places in the harness's command line.

repo.description: The repository to work in: anything `git clone` accepts, a URL or a local path. The runner clones it into workspace/. Empty, the workspace starts as an empty repository; for a turn it is the instance's own folder.

ref.description: What `git checkout` is given after the clone. A reader takes HEAD when it is empty or left out.

gate.description: The command that says pass or fail, as the program and its arguments. It runs in workspace/ with no shell, and the job passes when it exits zero. A turn in a conversation names none: it runs, and its evidence claims no verdict.

harness.description: The name of the adapter that runs the work, looked for in harnesses/ inside the job directory, then in the directory GUSTO_HARNESSES names, then among the built-in ones.

model.description: The model to ask for, put in place of {model} in the adapter. When empty or left out, the harness uses whatever it is configured with.

sensitivity.description: How sensitive the code is. Restricted code only talks to a model on this machine or a private network, and the runner refuses the job otherwise. A reader takes internal when it is empty or left out, and refuses any other label.

budget.description: What a job may spend before a runner stops it. A zero or missing member takes its default.

turns.description: The turns a harness may take. It is kept with the job; no runner enforces it yet, so the seconds are what stop a run.

seconds.description: The wall-clock seconds the harness may run. When they are spent the harness is killed and the manifest records stoppedAtBudget; the gate still runs.

usd.description: A cap on what the job's calls to a model may cost, in US dollars, counted at the proxy from the provider's own answers and the operator's prices. Once it is spent the proxy refuses the job's next call and the manifest records stoppedByCap. Left out, there is no cap; zero allows nothing. A reader refuses a negative cap. Only a job whose model is reached through the proxy is capped.

team.description: Who the job's spend counts against. A team named in the operator's spend policy has a monthly cap its jobs share. It is a label the person asking chooses; nothing yet proves they belong to the team.

session.description: The instance this job is a turn on. Its workspace is mounted instead of a clone of repo.

thread.description: The conversation on that instance this job is a turn in.

remembered.description: The harness's own name for that conversation, handed back so it resumes rather than starts again.

setup.description: The configuration the harness ran with: the names of its skills and of the MCP servers it could call. The definitions travel beside the job in setup/, outside the evidence, because a server's definition can carry a token.

gateway.description: The servers the job reached through the gateway, whose addresses and credentials stayed outside the sandbox.

integrations.description: Each integration the skills and servers came from, with the version that was on when the job started.
